title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages). f: X -> S is a holomorphic family, and the forms involved are relative 1-forms. A finite family mu = (D_i, omega_i), with D_i differential operators on S and omega_i relative closed 1-forms, is called a 'Picard-Fuchs equation' if sum_i D_i ∫_{Z_s} omega_i = 0 for every continuous family of 1-cycles Z_s. In that case, for two local sections a, b, the quantity mu(a,b) = sum_i D_i ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} omega_i is a well-defined holomorphic function on S. It is additive (cocycle) in (a,b), so it gives a homomorphism from sections, or points of the Jacobian, to functions on S. This is exactly the shape of Manin's map in the function-field Mordell problem.

This page looks for a manageable infinitesimal criterion that replaces the global vanishing on all cycles.

(6) Put Phi = f_*(Z Omega^1_{X/S}) / d f_*(O_X), i.e. relatively closed 1-forms modulo relative exact ones. This is the naive model of R^1 f_* Omega^._{X/S}; it agrees with that sheaf when the fibres have no higher coherent cohomology, e.g. affine or Stein fibres. Phi carries a natural integrable connection, the Gauss-Manin connection. It is computed by the Cartan formula: lift a vector field D on S locally to a vector field D-bar on X and take the Lie derivative L_{D-bar} = i d + d i. On closed forms this is d(i_{D-bar} omega) up to the horizontal part, which is independent of the lift modulo exact forms. The margin warns that this connection on Phi exists only under a hypothesis on X -> S (smooth, or 'stationary'; the word is uncertain).

Claim (7). It suffices that sum_i D_i omega_i = 0 in Phi, with D_i acting through Gauss-Manin.

Method.
- When X/S carries an integrable connection (a stratification), f_*(Omega^*_{X/S}) is also stratified.
- One lifts the D_i to operators D-bar_i on forms on X that commute with the relative differential d_{X/S}.
- The form varpi = sum_i D-bar_i omega_i is then again closed (8, renumbered).
- A crossed-out attempt writes D-bar_i = D-bar_i^o + c_i id, where D-bar_i^o has constant coefficients.

The next page completes the argument:
- In Phi, (7) means varpi = d phi locally over S.
- Differentiation under the integral, D ∫_{Z_s} omega = ∫_{Z_s} D-bar omega, gives sum_i D_i ∫_Z omega_i = ∫_Z d phi = 0 on cycles.
- On paths from a to b, it gives mu(a,b) = phi(b) - phi(a), i.e. an evaluation of a function at sections.

This is the mechanism of the Manin homomorphism: a Picard-Fuchs operator applied to an abelian integral yields an algebraic or holomorphic function of the point.
errors: Phi = f_*(ZOmega^1)/d f_*(O) equals relative de Rham H^1 only when the fibres have no H^1(O) (affine/Stein fibres). For proper curves this quotient is not H^1_dR, and the Gauss-Manin connection must be defined on the hypercohomology. The note implicitly works locally or with open curves.

A lift D-bar_i commuting with d_{X/S} exists only locally, e.g. via a local product structure or an integrable connection on X/S. The page's hypothesis 'X/S muni d'une connexion intégrable' is stronger than needed. Gauss-Manin needs only local lifts plus the Cartan homotopy formula.
The boxed formulas (8)-(9) with the decomposition D-bar = D-bar^o + c_i id are crossed out as wrong or unnecessary. The equation numbering is then reused: the final (8) is varpi.
mu(a,b) = phi(b) - phi(a) holds only up to the choice of path and of phi, which is determined up to functions pulled back from S. This is harmless since such functions cancel in the difference.

ideas.what: Gauss-Manin connection on relative H^1 via lifting vector fields and the Cartan formula L = i d + d i
ideas.where_published: 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) and 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), in substance

ideas.what: Infinitesimal criterion: sum D_i omega_i = 0 in H^1 under Gauss-Manin implies the operator kills all periods
ideas.modern_name: Picard-Fuchs equation as an element of the kernel of the D-module map

ideas.what: Picard-Fuchs operator applied to abelian integrals between two sections gives a well-defined additive function mu(a,b) = phi(b) - phi(a)
ideas.modern_name: Manin map / Manin homomorphism (theorem of the kernel)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin 1963; Coleman 1990; Chai 1991; Buium (differential algebraic version)

ideas.what: Differentiation under the integral sign over a continuous family of cycles, D ∫_Z omega = ∫_Z D-bar omega

missed.claim: Grothendieck worked out a personal, analytic-local version of the Manin homomorphism. A Picard-Fuchs relation in H^1 with Gauss-Manin makes sum D_i ∫_a^b omega_i equal to a difference phi(b) - phi(a) of a function evaluated at sections. This bears on Manin's function-field Mordell argument, whose 'theorem of the kernel' gap was only addressed by Coleman (1990) and Chai. The unpublished treatment is a historical datum rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: Je dis qu'il suffit qu'on ait (7) Σ D_i ω_i = 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's engagement with Manin's map in the 1970s; the mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard derivation of the Gauss-Manin/Picard-Fuchs criterion and of the Manin-map formula. Its interest is mostly historical, linking Grothendieck's Gauss-Manin notes to Manin's Mordell argument.
transcription_corrections: The margin note seems to read 'attention, une connexion sur Φ seulement si X → S stationnaire' (or similar). The last word is a long word, likely 'stationnaire' rather than 'lisse'.
'formes les D_i ω_i' is probably 'transformées' or 'formons les D_i ω_i'.
'{+on opérateurs+}' is probably 'en opérateurs' or 'des opérateurs D̄_i sur Ω*_X'.
The final displayed formula is Σ α_{D̄_i} ω_i = ϖ, renumbered (8) after the crossed-out block, and the word under the last line looks like 'aisément' or 'aussitôt' (uncertain).
In the first line, '(6)' labels the boxed definition Φ = f_*(ZΩ^1_{X/S}) / d f_*(O_X). The superscript is 1, not i.
